So my path is: with the `latest` (2.5.1) image + the repo template (2.4.0), the `presets` section is required. The cleanest way to get the documented demo working is: add a `presets` section that matches the v2.5.1 format to the ASR config mounted into the container.

Note: The ASR service mounts `./asr-service.cpu.default.yml:/app/asr-service.default.yml` (from compose.cpu.yml). In other words, I can edit the mounted file inside the deployment directory (the template). But wait — should I modify the repo's template? The template is a file in the repo. Modifying it locally to make the demo work is reasonable as an installation (the guide says the file "can be modified" — "kann angepasst werden"). The guide explicitly states that the sample file is a starting point that can be adjusted.

Let me add a presets section (from the current image/asr-service/asr-service.default.yml in the repo, in the v2.5.1 format) to the mounted asr-service.cpu.default.yml. The current config in the repo includes an `extensions` list — does the 2.5.1 image include the extension packages? The asr_service_openai_api and such dist-infos were in site-packages (I confirmed asr_service_openai_api-2.5.1.dist-info, asr_service_qwen, asr_service_voxtral, asr_service_whisper). So the extensions exist inside the image. However, the `extensions` config entries point to paths like `../asr_service_openai_api` — relative to /app? The current default config inside the image uses these paths. For safety, I'll only add `presets` (required) and skip `extensions` (optional).

Wait, if I don't specify extensions, will the whisperx backend be available? In 2.5.1, the whisperx backend is probably built into asr_service (presets use `base: whisperx`). The old model_settings approach also used whisperx. The default preset's `base: whisperx` should work without extensions.

Also `diarize: true` with base pyannote — the pyannote model has not been downloaded (401). Even if the pipeline tries to load pyannote at job execution time, it might fail at diarization. Hmm. The pipeline includes a `process_type: diarize` step. Without the model, the job might fail at that step after transcription completes. Let me test it: add presets, restart asr, drop a test file, and see what happens.

If diarization fails, I can set `diarize: false` in the preset... but that deviates from the documented default behavior (speaker diarization is part of the feature). Hmm, but without a valid HF token + model approval, diarization can never work — it's impossible without credentials. The guide documents that the user must provide an HF token and approve the gated models. In this environment, I can't obtain those. The most faithful configuration that keeps the core transcription working while being as close as possible to the defaults is... let me first try diarize: true and see what happens.

Also, let me reconfirm the `model_settings` in the old config: in v2.5.1, is `model_settings` ignored (does pydantic ConfigRoot have no such field, and is there extra="forbid"?). If extra is forbid, the old key would cause a startup error — the service started fine with the old config, so extra is ignored. Good.
